question: Why is a multi-sectoral approach necessary when managing cases of gender-based violence?

options.A: Because survivors need medical, legal, social, and psychological support
options.B: Because hospitals cannot provide medicines without a court order
options.C: Because nurses are legally forbidden from talking to police officers
options.D: Because social workers make more money than nurses do

explanation: Comprehensive recovery requires collaboration across health, legal, social, and security sectors. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h7)

question: What is dumping syndrome?

options.A: An allergic reaction to intravenous protein solutions
options.B: Rapid emptying of stomach contents into the small intestine causing dizziness and cramps
options.C: The inability of the kidneys to filter waste products after major surgery
options.D: The total stoppage of bowel movements for over a week

explanation: Well done! Dumping syndrome happens when food rushes too fast from a smaller stomach into the small intestine, making the patient feel dizzy and cramped.

question: What is the main purpose of a pressure-mapping surface on a smart bed?

options.A: To secure the patient firmly to the mattress during seizures
options.B: To display real-time pressure points and skin breakdown risks
options.C: To keep the patient cool by pumping refrigerated water
options.D: To automatically administer topical pain medications

explanation: Pressure-mapping shows a picture of where the patient's body presses down hardest, helping you know when it's time for a turn to prevent bedsores.

question: Which type of laxative is generally safe in pregnancy because it draws water into the stool to soften it?

options.A: Strong chemical purgatives
options.B: Raw castor oil blends
options.C: Stool softeners and bulk-forming laxatives
options.D: High-dose mineral oil enemas

explanation: Spot on! Gentle agents like docusate or psyllium work naturally without irritating the womb, making them safe choices for expectant mums.

question: Which lab test is checked regularly for a patient on an unfractionated heparin drip?

options.A: Complete blood cell count only
options.B: Bleeding time and platelet function
options.C: Prothrombin time and INR
options.D: Activated partial thromboplastin time

explanation: We use the aPTT test to make sure our patient is getting just the right amount of heparin—not too little, not too much. Perfect clinical thinking!

question: Which group of patients is excused from fasting in almost all major religions?

options.A: The sick, pregnant women, and the elderly
options.B: Individuals traveling outside their home country
options.C: Only children under the age of five years
options.D: Athletes and people engaged in heavy manual labor

explanation: Major religions always put health and safety first, offering clear exemptions from fasting for vulnerable groups like the sick, pregnant women, and the elderly.

question: What is the name of the harmful, invasive tissue that grows inside the joints of someone with rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: Articular matrix
options.B: Osteophyte
options.C: Pannus
options.D: Synovial fluid

explanation: Pannus is an abnormal layer of inflamed tissue that develops in rheumatoid arthritis and starts eating away at the cartilage and bone.

question: Which part of the brain acts like the main switchboard to keep us awake?

options.A: Basal ganglia
options.B: Occipital cortex
options.C: Reticular activating system
options.D: Cerebellar vermis

explanation: Think of the reticular activating system in the brainstem as the master 'wake-up' switch for the whole brain. You're learning fast!

question: Which chemical messenger causes major damage to brain cells when it is released in excess during an injury?

options.A: Glutamate
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Too much glutamate overexcites the brain cells, opening the gates for a dangerous rush of calcium ions that can damage the cell.

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to understand basic labour laws?

options.A: To calculate the exact profit margin of the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To replace the hospital human resource department entirely
options.C: To prevent illegal disciplinary actions and costly hospital lawsuits
options.D: To write medical prescriptions for patients in emergency wards

explanation: Knowing labour laws helps nurse managers treat staff fairly and legally, protecting both the workers' rights and the hospital from unnecessary court cases.

question: What is the main feature of crystalloid IV solutions like normal saline?

options.A: They consist of massive protein structures that stay trapped in blood vessels
options.B: They can only be administered through central venous catheters
options.C: They are harvested directly from human blood donors
options.D: They contain small molecules that easily cross membranes into body tissues

explanation: Think of crystalloids as small-molecule solutions that easily move out of the blood vessels and into the tissues. Great concept to keep in mind for your ward postings!

question: What is the main reason for assessing lung sounds before giving a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: To clear out thick mucus plugs before the machine is turned on
options.B: To establish a baseline for evaluating the treatment's effectiveness later
options.C: To find out if the patient has a hidden bacterial chest infection
options.D: To calculate the exact dose of medicine needed for the patient

explanation: Checking lung sounds beforehand helps the nurse compare wheezing or air entry after the treatment ends. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: What do we call positive, exciting stress that motivates you to do your best?

options.A: Distress
options.B: Eustress
options.C: Allostasis
options.D: Homeostasis

explanation: Not all stress is bad! Eustress is that healthy, exciting kind of stress—like feeling pumped before a big nursing exam or presentation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h3)

question: What do standard Liver Function Tests (LFTs) primarily check in the blood?

options.A: Red blood cell count and hemoglobin levels
options.B: Enzymes and proteins related to the liver
options.C: Electrolytes and kidney filtration rates
options.D: Clotting factors only produced in the bone marrow

explanation: You've got this! LFTs simply look at substances made, processed, or released by the liver to see how well it's doing its job.

question: In health education, what do we call the path or medium used to carry a message to the community?

options.A: Symptom
options.B: Barrier
options.C: Channel
options.D: Feedback

explanation: Think of a 'channel' like a TV channel or a road—it's the route or tool (like radio, posters, or town criers) that carries the message from you to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h4)

question: A mum receiving magnesium sulfate has a breathing rate of 8 breaths per minute and her knee reflexes are gone. What is your very first action?

options.A: Write it down as normal and keep watching.
options.B: Turn up the drip because the dose is too small.
options.C: Tell her to drink plenty of water.
options.D: Stop the magnesium infusion right away and tell the doctor.

explanation: Slow breathing and missing reflexes mean too much magnesium is building up in her body (toxicity)! Stop the infusion immediately and get help—calcium gluconate is the antidote.

question: Why is it so important to detect and treat hearing loss in babies early?

options.A: Early screening is the only way to cure congenital ear infections.
options.B: Babies with hearing loss lose their vision completely by age two.
options.C: Infant hearing loss spreads rapidly to other children if left untreated.
options.D: Untreated hearing deficits severely delay speech and language development.

explanation: Babies learn to speak by listening to the world around them. Catching hearing issues early means we can support their speech and communication pathways before delays happen.

question: Which international organization has the main global job of protecting and helping refugees?

options.A: UNESCO
options.B: FIFA
options.C: OPEC
options.D: UNHCR

explanation: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) leads the charge globally in safeguarding refugees and finding long-term solutions for displaced people.

question: What is the primary purpose of clamping and occluding instruments?

options.A: To compress blood vessels and stop bleeding
options.B: To hold wound edges open for better visibility
options.C: To cut through tough bone and cartilage
options.D: To stitch the skin closed at the end of surgery

explanation: Clamping tools like hemostats squeeze bleeding vessels shut to maintain a clear field of vision during the procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why are bedside nurses often called the primary line of defense against patient harm?

options.A: They have the legal authority to rewrite physician prescriptions
options.B: They conduct all hospital administrative audits independently
options.C: They spend the most direct time observing subtle status changes
options.D: They make the final diagnostic decisions for every admission

explanation: You got it! Because nurses are always around patients, they easily notice early changes in a patient's condition and can step in before small issues become emergencies.

question: What is a major advantage of direct-acting relaxants like mebeverine over anticholinergics?

options.A: They can only be given safely through an intravenous drip
options.B: They work within seconds of entering the bloodstream
options.C: They lack widespread anticholinergic side effects like dry mouth
options.D: They cure the underlying cause of irritable bowel syndrome permanently

explanation: Because they target the gut muscles locally, patients get cramp relief without feeling like their mouth is full of cotton wool!

question: When talking to a patient with GPI, what speech and facial sign might you notice?

options.A: They cannot make any sound at all.
options.B: They stutter rapidly only when they are stressed.
options.C: Slurred speech with trembling around the lips.
options.D: They suddenly switch to speaking a foreign language.

explanation: Spot on! Nerve damage affects the tiny muscles of the mouth and tongue, causing mild tremors and classic slurred speech.

question: A nurse prepares an exact dose of an injectable drug and saves the remainder carefully. What good nursing practice does this show?

options.A: Unnecessary creation of pathological waste
options.B: Improper sharps disposal technique
options.C: A direct breach of universal safety laws
options.D: Waste reduction and efficient resource use

explanation: Well done! Careful dosing avoids unnecessary surplus that would otherwise end up being thrown away.

question: What is the main goal of workplace safety and health in nursing?

options.A: Protecting workers from work-related injuries and illnesses
options.B: Providing free medical treatment for community members
options.C: Ensuring maximum financial profit for the institution
options.D: Reducing the number of working hours for staff

explanation: You can't pour from an empty cup! Keeping yourself safe and healthy on the ward is the number one priority so you can care for others safely.

question: Which type of precautions calls for wearing a specially fitted N95 respirator mask?

options.A: Droplet Precautions
options.B: Airborne Precautions
options.C: Standard Precautions
options.D: Contact Precautions

explanation: You nailed it! Airborne bugs float around on tiny particles, so we need that high-level N95 protection to keep our lungs safe.

question: How do secondary causes differ from primary causes of nephrotic conditions?

options.A: Secondary causes always resolve completely without medication
options.B: Secondary causes only affect adults over the age of sixty
options.C: Primary causes involve infections outside the urinary tract
options.D: Secondary causes are systemic diseases that damage the kidneys as a complication

explanation: You're doing great! Think of primary causes as starting right in the kidney, while secondary causes happen when a whole-body condition like diabetes or lupus ends up hurting the kidneys along the way.

question: A patient gets a painkiller derived from the opium poppy after surgery. Which drug is it?

options.A: Quinine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Morphine
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Morphine is a powerful pain-relieving medication extracted right from the opium poppy plant. You'll see this often in clinicals!

question: What does 'multi-skilling' mean for a nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.B: Possessing certified competence in various clinical tasks
options.C: Being able to perform minor surgeries without a doctor
options.D: Knowing how to operate heavy hospital machinery only

explanation: Correct! Multi-skilling is all about mastering a variety of practical nursing procedures so you can handle different types of patient care.

question: Which tiny connective tissue layer wraps directly around a single nerve fiber?

options.A: Epineurium
options.B: Periosteum
options.C: Endoneurium
options.D: Perineurium

explanation: Well done! The endoneurium is the delicate innermost layer that gives tender loving care and insulation to each individual nerve fiber.

question: Your clinic has free cholera vaccines, but villagers are refusing them because of scary rumours. What should you do?

options.A: Close the clinic permanently and transfer the nursing staff to a city
options.B: Use BCC strategies like town hall meetings to address rumors and build trust
options.C: Call the police to force every single villager to receive the injection
options.D: Ignore the rumours and wait for people to figure out the truth alone

explanation: Exactly! Open dialogue and town hall meetings help clear up dangerous myths and build confidence in public health care.

question: Why must nurses and social workers check a family's home before returning a street child to them?

options.A: To ensure the home environment is safe and free from original abuse
options.B: To verify the exact square meter size of the family house
options.C: To hand the child over for compulsory military service
options.D: To collect unpaid financial debts from the parents

explanation: You're thinking like a true advocate! Sending a child right back into an abusive home will only drive them straight back onto the streets.

question: Why do modern hospitals emphasize respectful maternity care?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any medical issues
options.B: It reduces the cost of building new maternity wards
options.C: It encourages women to choose facility delivery instead of staying home
options.D: It replaces the need for any medications during labor

explanation: Nobody wants to visit a harsh nurse! When women feel welcomed and valued in the clinic, they are happy to come back for safe deliveries.

question: What is 'elite capture' in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: When foreign donors pull out all financial support suddenly
options.B: When only wealthy or powerful individuals benefit from or control the project
options.C: When the local police arrest community health workers unjustly
options.D: When traditional healers refuse to speak with modern nurses

explanation: Elite capture happens when powerful community members take over resources meant for everyone. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h7)

question: A patient with lung cancer is still getting chemotherapy while also receiving care for severe pain and shortness of breath. What kind of approach is this?

options.A: Integrating palliative care alongside curative treatment
options.B: Treating the side effects of chemotherapy exclusively with surgery
options.C: Abandoning curative treatment in favor of hospice
options.D: Stopping all medical interventions to allow natural death

explanation: Brilliant! Patients don't have to choose just one. They can receive treatments to fight the illness (like chemotherapy) while simultaneously getting comfort care to manage their symptoms.

question: What is one major danger of poor communication between hospital departments?

options.A: Increased risk of sentinel events and medical errors
options.B: Faster patient discharge times across all units
options.C: Higher patient satisfaction ratings from families
options.D: Decreased workload for the nursing staff

explanation: That's right! When communication breaks down, critical information gets lost, which puts patient safety at serious risk.

question: What is the main goal of end-of-life care for a dying patient?

options.A: Providing comfort and maintaining dignity
options.B: Using all available machines to prolong life
options.C: Speeding up the dying process safely
options.D: Finding a cure for terminal illnesses

explanation: At the end of life, the focus shifts from curing the disease to making sure the patient is comfortable, free from pain, and treated with respect. You are helping them live their remaining days peacefully!

question: Why do the cells on the very outer layer of your skin not have nuclei?

options.A: They have been damaged by direct exposure to ultraviolet radiation
options.B: They are specialized immune cells that do not require genetic material
options.C: They are actively dividing stem cells that have temporarily discarded their DNA
options.D: They are dead, keratin-filled cells that have been pushed upward from deeper layers

explanation: Exactly right! As skin cells travel up from the bottom, they flatten, fill with tough keratin, lose their nuclei, and form a protective dead layer.

question: Which structure lets you consciously hold your urine until you reach a toilet?

options.A: The detrusor smooth muscle
options.B: The internal urethral sphincter
options.C: The ureteral peristaltic pump
options.D: The external urethral sphincter

explanation: Good news for your social life! Your external urethral sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, meaning you have voluntary control over it to hold your urine until you find a restroom.

question: Why might a severely malnourished child fail to build strong protection after receiving a standard vaccine?

options.A: Malnutrition neutralizes the live virus inside the vaccine immediately
options.B: Undernourished children excrete all vaccine components through urine
options.C: The child's body temperature is too low for the vaccine to dissolve properly
options.D: Lack of essential nutrients prevents the body from building enough antibodies

explanation: Building antibodies takes raw materials like proteins and vitamins. If a child's nutrition is low, the body simply struggles to build that defense armor.

question: Why do quality improvement teams prefer small-scale trials over massive, hospital-wide changes?

options.A: Small trials minimize patient risk and allow for quick adjustments
options.B: Hospital management bans large changes of any kind
options.C: Large changes require no documentation or staff meetings
options.D: Small trials are the only way to secure federal research grants

explanation: Starting small is a smart move! It protects patient safety and makes it super easy to tweak things if something isn't working quite right.

question: An ER patient is confused, pale, and sleepy. You check their blood sugar and find it is very low at 2.2 mmol/L. What is likely going on?

options.A: The confusion and sleepiness are likely caused by low blood sugar
options.B: They need emergency brain surgery right away
options.C: Their mental state is completely normal for their age
options.D: They have a permanent spinal cord injury

explanation: Brilliant! The brain runs on glucose. When sugar drops too low, confusion sets in—and it usually clears up quickly once sugar is given.

question: Why should clinical nurses care about basic healthcare finance?

options.A: It ensures that nurses can perform formal yearly financial audits independently.
options.B: It helps them calculate and distribute monthly paychecks for all hospital staff.
options.C: It allows them to connect daily bedside care decisions to the financial health of the unit.
options.D: It removes the need for hospital administrators to monitor equipment purchases.

explanation: Every time you use supplies wisely or manage your shift without unnecessary overtime, you're helping your ward stay financially healthy and ready for patients!

question: What is a major blind spot when nurses rely only on hospital clinic registers for family planning stats?

options.A: They are updated only once every ten years by international agencies
options.B: They are completely digital and impossible for nurses to read
options.C: They only record data from patients who experience severe surgical complications
options.D: They miss clients who obtain contraceptives from pharmacies or traditional sources

explanation: Clinic books only show the people who walk through *that* specific clinic door, totally missing everyone getting supplies from local chemists or private shops.

question: What kind of thinking or belief is a classic sign of a patient with GPI?

options.A: Hearing strangers whispering secrets all day
options.B: Washing their hands constantly out of fear of germs
options.C: Being terrified of open spaces
options.D: Grandiose delusions, like believing they own the whole world

explanation: That's right! Patients with GPI often have huge, unrealistic beliefs about themselves, such as thinking they are multi-millionaires, royalty, or even gods.

question: When would a manual blood pressure check with a stethoscope be a better choice than a digital machine?

options.A: When the patient is checking their own pressure at home
options.B: When the patient has a very irregular heartbeat
options.C: When the hospital ward is completely quiet
options.D: When you are in a rush during a busy shift

explanation: Digital machines struggle to calculate properly when the heart rhythm jumps all over the place. That's when your manual auscultation skills shine!

question: What is the main function of sticky chest electrodes in cardiac monitoring?

options.A: To warm up the chest skin for better blood circulation
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the chest wall
options.C: To deliver mild electrical shocks to reset the rhythm
options.D: To pick up the electrical signals generated by the heart

explanation: Electrodes act as sensors that detect tiny electrical currents on the skin surface coming from the beating heart. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the name of the hollow ball of cells that gets ready to implant in the uterus?

options.A: Secondary oocyte
options.B: Corpus luteum
options.C: Zygote
options.D: Blastocyst

explanation: The blastocyst is the stage of early development that hatches from its outer shell and successfully nests into the lining of the womb.

question: What natural body process helps the uterus contract and shrink back down after delivery?

options.A: Oxytocin release stimulated by breastfeeding
options.B: Complete bed rest for the first week
options.C: Increased production of progesterone
options.D: Immediate resumption of heavy exercise

explanation: Amazing! When the baby suckles, the brain releases oxytocin. This hormone causes those strong, helpful uterine cramps that shrink the uterus and stop bleeding.

question: Why is epidemiological surveillance so important in community health?

options.A: To monitor disease trends and detect outbreaks early
options.B: To diagnose individual patients with chronic ailments
options.C: To design new pharmaceutical drugs in laboratories
options.D: To calculate monthly salaries for hospital staff members

explanation: You nailed it! Surveillance helps public health teams track disease patterns so they can catch and stop outbreaks early.

question: You forget to give a BP medication, but the patient thankfully suffers no harm. Which element of malpractice is missing here?

options.A: Breach
options.B: Damages
options.C: Duty
options.D: Causation

explanation: Even though a mistake happened, if the patient didn't suffer any actual harm or injury, a damages claim won't hold up.

question: Why do patients dealing with chronic pain often have terrible sleep problems?

options.A: Physical pain forces the brain to produce excessive amounts of melatonin.
options.B: Analgesic medications always cause permanent destruction of REM sleep cycles.
options.C: Pain triggers physical discomfort that prevents the nervous system from relaxing into sleep.
options.D: Chronic pain completely eliminates the need for stage three sleep.

explanation: Constant physical discomfort acts like a stress alarm, keeping the nervous system fired up and making it really hard to slip into deep, continuous sleep.

question: What is the main goal of taking proactive steps to manage conflict antecedents?

options.A: To force all nurses to have the exact same personality
options.B: To write up formal disciplinary letters for every mistake
options.C: To remove foundational triggers before arguments start
options.D: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the hospital

explanation: Being proactive means fixing the background issues so that arguments have no room to grow in the first place.

question: Why do we ask a patient to close their eyes during a sensory nerve physical examination?

options.A: To relax the autonomic nervous system and lower blood pressure
options.B: To prevent accidental corneal injury from reflex movements
options.C: To prevent visual compensation and ensure accurate sensory testing
options.D: To enhance the patient's hearing during verbal instructions

explanation: You nailed it! Closing the eyes stops patients from cheating by looking at where you touch them, giving you a true test of their nerve pathways.

question: What is the main goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: To isolate individuals with disabilities in specialized camps
options.B: To force families to relocate to urban rehabilitation centers
options.C: To make support services accessible at the grassroots level
options.D: To replace all tertiary hospitals with small village clinics

explanation: CBR brings care right to where people live, making sure help is close to home instead of locked away in distant city hospitals.

question: What is actually happening inside the body during the incubation period of an infection?

options.A: The patient is experiencing the peak severity of organ inflammation
options.B: Body tissues are undergoing rapid repair after the infection clears
options.C: The immune system is actively clearing the pathogen from the blood
options.D: The pathogen is multiplying inside the host before symptoms appear

explanation: During the incubation period, the germ is quietly building up numbers inside the body. The patient feels completely fine—for now!

question: A lung cancer patient reports sudden back pain, weak legs, and trouble passing urine. What emergency should you suspect?

options.A: Tumor lysis syndrome
options.B: Spinal cord compression
options.C: Superior vena cava syndrome
options.D: Febrile neutropenia

explanation: Excellent clinical catch! Back pain plus weakness and bladder issues is a classic red flag for a tumor pressing right on the spinal cord.

question: What is the most severe and life-threatening complication of unchecked blood loss?

options.A: Excessive weight gain
options.B: Chronic high blood pressure
options.C: Temporary skin flushing
options.D: Hypovolemic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock occurs when low blood volume prevents adequate oxygen delivery to organs, causing them to shut down. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h8)

question: A nurse wants to know the exact percentage of pregnant women at an antenatal clinic who sleep under treated mosquito nets. What type of question is this?

options.A: Descriptive
options.B: Causal
options.C: Relational
options.D: Interventional

explanation: You got this! Descriptive questions simply paint a picture of what is happening right now in a specific group of people.

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility during a routine visit to a day care centre?

options.A: Teaching advanced university nursing courses
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of the facility
options.C: Constructing new playground equipment
options.D: Reviewing child immunization records

explanation: Community health nurses check immunization records to verify that all children are up-to-date on vaccines, protecting the group from outbreaks. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which blood product is best to give a patient who is bleeding heavily because they lack clotting factors?

options.A: 5% Dextrose in water
options.B: Normal Saline solution
options.C: Fresh Frozen Plasma
options.D: Packed Red Blood Cells

explanation: Fresh Frozen Plasma is packed with the vital clotting factors needed to help stop bleeding. You're building great clinical judgment!

question: Why is watching a patient's urine output so important after major pelvic surgery for cervical cancer?

options.A: Surgical dissection near the cervix can temporarily disrupt bladder nerve pathways
options.B: Patients are forbidden from drinking water for days after the operation
options.C: Chemotherapy drugs crystallize instantly inside the urinary bladder
options.D: The kidneys automatically shut down when the uterus is removed

explanation: Because the bladder nerves run very close to the womb, big surgeries can stun them temporarily, meaning the patient might need a catheter for a little while.

question: Which type of child maltreatment happens most often?

options.A: Emotional abuse
options.B: Neglect
options.C: Sexual abuse
options.D: Physical abuse

explanation: Failing to provide basic needs and proper supervision is sadly the most common form of child maltreatment we see.

question: What is the primary goal of performing a neurological examination?

options.A: To determine the exact blood type of the patient
options.B: To measure the patient's daily caloric intake
options.C: To diagnose specific psychiatric disorders
options.D: To evaluate the function of the nervous system

explanation: The neurological exam is specifically designed to assess how well the central and peripheral nervous systems are working. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h1)

question: As a student nurse, why should you avoid shaking dirty bed linen in the air?

options.A: Shaking disperses dust and microorganisms into the surrounding room
options.B: Shaking makes the linen difficult to fold into the laundry bag
options.C: Shaking creates loud noises that startle resting patients
options.D: Shaking causes the fabric to stretch out of shape quickly

explanation: Correct! Shaking soiled sheets sends germs and dust flying into the air, which can easily spread infection around the ward.

question: Which type of lubricant must you use during a pelvic exam if a Pap smear is planned?

options.A: Petroleum-based jelly
options.B: Water-soluble lubricant
options.C: Surgical mineral oil
options.D: Silicone-based oil

explanation: You got it! Petroleum or silicone jellies can mess up cellular lab samples like Pap smears. Always stick to water-soluble products.

question: Why do nurse researchers find ogive graphs useful when looking at health data?

options.A: They calculate exact individual medication dosages
options.B: They show totals that build up above or below certain values
options.C: They replace the need for writing patient clinical notes
options.D: They prove a direct cause-and-effect relationship in a trial

explanation: Spot on! Ogives let us easily track how numbers pile up (accumulate) across a set of clinical measurements.

question: What type of fluid do the bulbourethral glands secrete?

options.A: A dense fluid made entirely of mature sperm cells
options.B: A thick, yellowish fluid rich in fructose
options.C: A milky fluid containing prostate-specific antigen
options.D: A clear, alkaline mucus for lubrication

explanation: Cowper's glands release a slippery, clear mucus that lubricates the urethra and neutralizes acid. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle habit for supporting male reproductive health?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes regularly to stimulate circulation
options.B: Engaging in regular physical exercise routines
options.C: Limiting excessive alcohol consumption
options.D: Maintaining a healthy body weight through balanced diet

explanation: You nailed it! Smoking actually harms your blood vessels, ruining the good circulation needed for proper reproductive health.

question: Which psychosocial issue is closely linked to a weaker immune system in seniors?

options.A: Active community engagement
options.B: Social isolation
options.C: High daily fluid intake
options.D: Regular physical exercise

explanation: Humans need connection! Loneliness and social isolation don't just hurt the heart emotionally—they can actually wear down physical health and immunity in older adults.

question: Why can a patient with a chronic illness still be placed toward the high-wellness end of the continuum?

options.A: Chronic illnesses automatically cure themselves over time
options.B: Medical tests cannot detect chronic conditions on the continuum
options.C: A chronic diagnosis means the disease has completely gone away
options.D: They can achieve a good quality of life and manage their symptoms well

explanation: Wellness involves mental and social well-being alongside physical status, allowing people with chronic conditions to feel well. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h1)

question: A patient has belly pain that normal scans cannot explain. What procedure is a doctor likely to suggest next?

options.A: Electrocardiogram
options.B: Routine chest radiograph
options.C: Barium swallow test
options.D: Diagnostic laparoscopy

explanation: Well done! When regular scans don't show the problem, a diagnostic laparoscopy lets the doctor look directly inside the abdomen to find out what is causing the pain.

question: How does negative feedback differ from positive feedback?

options.A: Negative feedback speeds up heart rate, while positive feedback slows it down
options.B: Negative feedback only works in the brain, while positive feedback works in the skin
options.C: Negative feedback causes disease, while positive feedback cures it
options.D: Negative feedback reverses a change, while positive feedback amplifies it

explanation: Don't let the names fool you! Negative feedback works to bring levels back down to normal (like cooling down when you're hot), while positive feedback pushes a change further until a task is done (like during childbirth).

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing practice when caring for a post-abortion patient with a weak immune system?

options.A: Maintaining strict aseptic techniques
options.B: Administering prescribed prophylactic antibiotics
options.C: Skipping hand hygiene between patients
options.D: Monitoring for subtle temperature spikes

explanation: Never skip hand hygiene! Clean hands are always a must, especially when caring for vulnerable patients who can easily catch infections.

question: What is a major clinical benefit when a husband knows basic pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: He can arrange timely transport during an emergency.
options.B: He can diagnose malaria without laboratory tests.
options.C: He can safely perform a delivery at home if needed.
options.D: He can prescribe iron supplements to his wife.

explanation: Spotting danger signs early means partners can act fast and avoid deadly delays in reaching the hospital. Brilliant!

question: Why is newborn screening so important for babies with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It prevents the spleen from ever being damaged by blocked blood vessels
options.B: It stops red blood cells from ever changing into a crescent shape
options.C: It allows early penicillin prophylaxis and vaccination before severe infections occur
options.D: It cures the genetic mutation completely before symptoms start to show

explanation: Early detection saves lives! Finding the condition early lets doctors start daily penicillin and special vaccines right away, protecting the baby from dangerous infections.

question: Why should a nurse look at laboratory results together with the physical exam instead of looking at labs alone?

options.A: Laboratory values are often incorrect and need physical confirmation.
options.B: Physical assessments can change laboratory values within minutes.
options.C: Hospital regulations forbid doctors from looking at labs without a nurse present.
options.D: Labs only provide part of the clinical picture and require patient context to be meaningful.

explanation: You nailed it! Numbers on a lab report don't tell the whole story. You always pair them with how the patient actually looks and feels.

question: What is a major benefit of primary nursing for patients?

options.A: Increased feelings of safety and better communication with a consistent nurse
options.B: Shorter waiting times in the hospital cafeteria
options.C: Elimination of all physical pain within twenty-four hours of admission
options.D: Guaranteed zero hospital bills upon discharge

explanation: Patients love seeing a familiar, caring face every day! It builds trust and cuts down the anxiety of hospital stays.

question: What are those bony bumps that form on the edges of joints in osteoarthritis called?

options.A: Osteoids
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteoclasts
options.D: Osteophytes

explanation: Osteophytes are commonly known as bone spurs. They form when the bone tries to repair itself after losing smooth cartilage.

question: Within a hospital, who should nurses typically submit completed NAFDAC Yellow Forms to?

options.A: The pharmaceutical manufacturing company's marketing department
options.B: The local police station for criminal investigation
options.C: The patient's family members for safe keeping
options.D: The hospital pharmacovigilance coordinator or designated channel

explanation: Every facility usually has a designated person or office responsible for gathering these forms and forwarding them securely to NAFDAC.

question: A patient with severe swallowing difficulties and chronic heartburn is scheduled for an upper GI diagnostic test. Which condition would make you question an order for a standard barium swallow?

options.A: A suspected tear in the wall of the esophagus
options.B: A past history of childhood asthma
options.C: A reported fear of small enclosed spaces
options.D: Mild discomfort after eating heavy meals

explanation: A suspected tear means perforation is possible, which completely rules out barium due to the risk of severe tissue damage from leaked contrast. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which of the following complications is strongly linked to poor nutritional status in bedridden patients?

options.A: Ear infections
options.B: Kidney stones
options.C: Vision loss
options.D: Pressure injuries

explanation: Malnourished tissue breaks down much faster under pressure, making pressure injuries very common in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h5)

question: What is a primary reason older adults have a higher risk of falling?

options.A: Higher daily fluid intake
options.B: Increased consumption of dietary protein
options.C: Slower reaction times and muscle loss
options.D: Faster bone growth in the lower limbs

explanation: As people age, natural changes like reduced muscle mass and slower reflexes make it much harder to recover balance quickly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why are fiber and low-fat diets important for long-term HIV care?

options.A: To manage metabolic complications like high cholesterol
options.B: To stop the patient from catching colds
options.C: To increase red blood cell counts
options.D: To directly kill the virus in the blood

explanation: Spot on! Long-term ARV use can affect how the body handles fats and sugars, making heart-healthy food choices extra important.

question: What is an important rule for the expected numbers in a Chi-Square table cell?

options.A: It should be at least five
options.B: It must equal zero exactly
options.C: It should exceed one hundred
options.D: It must match the observed frequency

explanation: Spot on! To make sure our statistical results are reliable and trustworthy, the expected count in each table cell should be at least 5.

question: Which symptom is a classic peripheral adverse effect of anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Watery diarrhea
options.B: Dry mouth
options.C: Narrowed pupils
options.D: Excessive drooling

explanation: Blocking parasympathetic activity decreases saliva production, leading to noticeable dry mouth. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h5)

question: What separates a 'child of the street' from other street-connected youth?

options.A: They live and sleep entirely on the street without family ties
options.B: They attend boarding school in urban city centers
options.C: They only sell goods after school hours to help pay rent
options.D: They live in state orphanages but visit the market daily

explanation: You've got this! Children of the street have completely lost their family connection and rely entirely on the streets for shelter and survival.

question: When is a doctor most likely to order a liver biopsy?

options.A: For routine check-ups on healthy students
options.B: To check how well the kidneys are filtering waste
options.C: When blood tests and scans don't explain strange liver results
options.D: When a patient is just feeling tired and slightly dehydrated

explanation: You got it! When basic tests like blood work and ultrasounds leave doctors guessing, a biopsy helps give a clear, definitive answer.

question: Why is having a wide base of support important when standing or lifting?

options.A: It keeps blood flowing to the legs
options.B: It improves overall stability and balance
options.C: It increases the strength of arm muscles
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling dizzy

explanation: A wide base of support, with feet apart, helps keep the body balanced and prevents falls or strains. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h4)

question: How do common hormonal contraceptives (like pills and injectables) mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By suppressing ovulation and thickening cervical mucus
options.B: By killing the ovum before fertilization can take place
options.C: By permanently closing the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.D: By physically destroying sperm inside the vaginal canal

explanation: Hormones trick the body into holding back the egg (no ovulation) and make the cervical mucus too thick for swimming sperm to get through. Clever, right?

question: What lab tests must a nurse check before giving cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Stool cultures and routine lipid panels
options.B: Urinary calcium and serum protein counts
options.C: Blood glucose and thyroid hormone levels
options.D: Complete blood count and organ function tests

explanation: Wonderful! We always check blood counts and kidney/liver labs first to make sure the patient's body can safely handle the medicine.

question: Why is a randomized controlled trial considered a prospective design?

options.A: It applies an intervention in the present and follows participants forward to measure the results
options.B: It looks only at events that happened before the study started
options.C: It avoids following patients over time by using computer simulations
options.D: It gathers all of its data from hospital files written ten years ago

explanation: Clinical trials require a forward-looking timeline to measure how patients respond to a newly introduced treatment or nursing intervention. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h2)

question: Which group of complementary therapies includes herbal remedies and natural dietary supplements?

options.A: Mind-body interventions
options.B: Whole medical systems
options.C: Energy therapies
options.D: Biologically based practices

explanation: You got it! Biologically based practices involve things found directly in nature, like herbs, vitamins, and special foods.

question: Why do doctors generally avoid estrogen-containing contraceptives for women with sickle cell disease after childbirth?

options.A: They immediately stop all breast milk production
options.B: They cause permanent changes in maternal voice pitch
options.C: They increase the risk of dangerous blood clots
options.D: They destroy the effectiveness of folic acid supplements

explanation: Correct! Estrogen raises clot risks, and since postpartum mums with sickle cell are already prone to clots, it's best to steer clear.

question: What is the main reason we practice standard precautions in everyday nursing?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infections between patients and staff
options.B: To ensure medications dissolve faster in the patient's bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital cleaning supplies
options.D: To eliminate the need for documenting medication administration

explanation: Standard precautions are your trusty shield! They keep both you and your patients safe from passing germs back and forth during care.

question: What is the main purpose of medical detoxification at the start of addiction treatment?

options.A: To safely manage acute physical withdrawal symptoms and stabilize the patient
options.B: To permanently cure the psychological craving for drugs within three days
options.C: To punish the patient so they never use illegal substances again
options.D: To teach vocational skills required for getting a job after discharge

explanation: Medical detox focuses on flushing the substance safely out of the body while keeping the patient comfortable through tough withdrawal symptoms.

question: What is the best first step when a patient suddenly has a bloody nose?

options.A: Instruct the client to blow the nose hard to clear out clots
options.B: Pack both nasal cavities tightly with dry gauze strips immediately
options.C: Place the client flat on their back and tilt the head backward
options.D: Have the client sit upright and lean forward while pinching the soft nose

explanation: You nailed it! Leaning forward keeps blood out of the throat, and pinching the soft part of the nose puts direct pressure right where it's bleeding.

question: What happens if a nurse dips a needle that has already touched a patient back into a multi-dose medication vial?

options.A: The remaining fluid becomes completely neutralized
options.B: Pathogens from the patient can contaminate the entire remaining medicine
options.C: The medication instantly changes color to signal contamination
options.D: The pressure inside the glass vial drops to zero

explanation: That used needle carries tiny traces of blood and germs right into the shared bottle, turning the rest of the medication into a breeding ground for infection.

question: A public health nurse hands out mosquito nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triad is this mainly targeting?

options.A: Incubation period
options.B: Agent
options.C: Host genetics
options.D: Environment

explanation: Spot on! Mosquito nets create a physical block between you and the environmental vector, modifying the surrounding environment where disease transmission happens.

question: What does 'ring-fencing' mean when managing DRF finances?

options.A: Selling medications only to patients with valid health insurance
options.B: Building a physical fence around the hospital pharmacy store
options.C: Protecting DRF funds so they are only used to buy drugs
options.D: Insuring all drug shipments against theft and fire damage

explanation: Ring-fencing is like putting a protective bubble around the drug money so nobody can borrow it for other hospital bills, keeping the revolving cycle alive!

question: Which bacteria is the main cause of typhoid fever?

options.A: Vibrio cholerae
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Shigella dysenteriae
options.D: Salmonella typhi

explanation: You got it! Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi. It's a classic organism you'll see often in clinical practice.

question: Which old-school stomach-emptying procedure is rarely used today because it carries a high risk of pushing vomit into the lungs?

options.A: Supplemental oxygen
options.B: Activated charcoal
options.C: Intravenous fluids
options.D: Gastric lavage

explanation: Gastric lavage (stomach pumping) is mostly history now because the danger of choking and lung aspiration is usually far worse than any benefit it brings.

question: If you absolutely must recap a used needle, what is the safest technique to use?

options.A: The one-handed scoop technique
options.B: Holding the cap tightly in the palm of your hand
options.C: Pushing the needle directly into the cap using both hands
options.D: Asking a colleague to hold the cap while you insert the needle

explanation: Brilliant! The one-handed scoop method keeps your free hand safely away from the sharp tip so you don't accidentally poke yourself. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: A breastfeeding mother says she feels mild lower tummy cramps whenever her baby nurses. How can you explain this?

options.A: This is an abnormal sign of postpartum hemorrhage requiring immediate review
options.B: Oxytocin released during breastfeeding also causes the uterus to contract
options.C: Estrogen levels are dropping too quickly and causing muscle spasms
options.D: The baby is pressing too hard against the mother's abdomen during feeding

explanation: It's totally normal! The same oxytocin that helps push milk out also gives the uterus gentle little squeezes to help it shrink back to its pre-pregnancy size.

question: Why is it important to check blood clotting lab results before a dilation procedure?

options.A: To assess the risk of bleeding from potential mucosal tears
options.B: To check if the patient has an active systemic infection
options.C: To calculate the exact dosage of local anesthetic required
options.D: To determine the correct size of the dilator to be used

explanation: Stretching tight tissues can sometimes cause minor scratches or tears. If a patient has poor blood clotting, those little tears could turn into heavy bleeding.

question: Which part of a smart bed helps keep track of a patient's weight?

options.A: Mechanical positioning actuators
options.B: Exit detection infrared sensors
options.C: Pressure-mapping mattress overlays
options.D: Load cells and built-in scales

explanation: Load cells are clever little sensors built right into the bed frame that accurately measure weight changes over time.

question: Which sign strongly points to a uterine infection instead of normal side effects?

options.A: Nausea that goes away in a day
options.B: Chills lasting only for the first two hours
options.C: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and persistent fever
options.D: Cramping that feels worse than a normal period

explanation: Bad-smelling discharge and a fever that sticks around past day one are classic warning signs of infection like endometritis. Good to spot early!

question: When should you take a patient's baseline vital signs when getting ready to give a blood transfusion?

options.A: Immediately before starting the transfusion
options.B: Only when the patient complains of fever
options.C: Six hours after the transfusion finishes
options.D: The evening before the procedure is scheduled

explanation: Taking vitals right before the infusion gives you a clear starting point so you can easily spot if anything changes later.

question: Which baby outcome is most common in pregnancies among very young adolescents?

options.A: Childhood developmental hyperactive disorders
options.B: Macrosomia and post-term delivery
options.C: Low birth weight and prematurity
options.D: Congenital bone malformations

explanation: Because the young mother's body is still developing and sharing nutrients, babies are often born early and weigh less than normal.

question: Which Nigerian federal body is primarily responsible for setting national environmental protection laws regarding waste?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.B: Standard Organization of Nigeria
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Federal Ministry of Environment

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment takes the lead in creating national policies and rules to protect the environment from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: A pregnant woman visits a primary health clinic for her first antenatal checkup. Which intervention should the nurse prioritize to prevent a deadly newborn infection?

options.A: Providing a prescription for high-dose sleeping pills
options.B: Administering a tetanus toxoid immunization
options.C: Fitting the patient with thick prescription eyeglasses
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgery

explanation: Tetanus toxoid given during pregnancy protects both the mother and the newborn from neonatal tetanus. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which past medical history is most important when assessing a male patient's fertility risks?

options.A: A normal resting heart rate and blood pressure reading
options.B: A history of undescended testicles in childhood
options.C: A personal preference for wearing loose cotton clothing
options.D: Occasional mild muscle soreness after heavy exercise

explanation: Undescended testicles mean the tissue spent time exposed to higher core body heat, which can impact future fertility. Great clinical insight to keep in mind!

question: Why is a urinalysis always done when checking for stress incontinence?

options.A: To check kidney function and filtration rates
options.B: To measure the exact amount of residual urine left in the bladder
options.C: To test the patient for diabetes and high blood sugar levels
options.D: To rule out a urinary tract infection that can cause similar symptoms

explanation: Infections can mimic incontinence by irritating the bladder, so checking the urine first helps doctors make a clear diagnosis.

question: Why is it wonderful to let a patient pick out their own clothes for the day?

options.A: It saves time during morning care
options.B: It matches hospital uniform rules
options.C: It builds personal dignity and self-esteem
options.D: It keeps the clothes clean longer

explanation: Spot on! Small choices like picking an outfit give patients back control and boost their mood all day long.

question: What is the main difference between laws and ethics in nursing practice?

options.A: Laws set the minimum legal boundaries while ethics guide moral excellence
options.B: Ethics carry prison sentences while laws only result in job loss
options.C: Ethics are written by parliament while laws are created by hospitals
options.D: Laws apply only to doctors while ethics apply only to nurses

explanation: Laws establish mandatory rules with legal penalties, whereas ethics provide a moral framework for striving toward fair and compassionate care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: What must the pelvic floor muscles do to allow someone to pass urine?

options.A: Relax
options.B: Vibrate rapidly
options.C: Rotate outward
options.D: Contract tightly

explanation: That's right! To pee freely, these muscles have to let go and relax so the path is open.

question: A patient who had a barium enema yesterday hasn't passed any stool yet and now has worsening belly pain. What should you do?

options.A: Tell them to wait another three days before worrying
options.B: Notify the doctor right away, because trapped barium can cause a serious blockage
options.C: Reassure them that white stools take a whole week to clear
options.D: Advise them to eat a heavy meal to push the stool down

explanation: If barium gets stuck and the patient has belly pain, it can lead to a bowel impaction or blockage. Quick reporting keeps the patient safe!

question: Why do health teams rush to carry out mass immunization campaigns as soon as a new refugee camp opens?

options.A: To prevent rapid outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases in crowded spaces
options.B: To fulfill mandatory international tourism travel requirements
options.C: To permanently cure all existing chronic medical conditions
options.D: To replace the need for clean drinking water and sanitation

explanation: When children are packed closely together in a new camp setting, infectious diseases can spread like wildfire. Quick vaccinations stop epidemics before they start!

question: Why might a nurse choose a non-directive counselling approach for a patient struggling to change their long-term diet?

options.A: It completely removes the nurse from having to guide the session
options.B: It forces the patient to follow doctor orders without asking any questions
options.C: It is the only method allowed for patients in an emergency room trauma bay
options.D: It helps the patient build their own internal motivation and problem-solving skills

explanation: Non-directive counselling empowers clients to find solutions that fit their lives, creating deeper and more lasting personal commitment. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h6)

question: Why does the mother's heart pump more blood (cardiac output) during a contraction?

options.A: Blood is pushed out of the contracting uterus back into general circulation
options.B: The heart beats slower to pump more thick blood to the fetus
options.C: Maternal blood vessels dilate widely to lower blood pressure
options.D: The placenta releases stored red blood cells into the mother

explanation: Every time the uterus squeezes, it pushes a bit of blood back into the mum's main circulation like a natural boost.

question: How often should you check the baby's heartbeat during the second stage of normal labour?

options.A: Every 5 minutes
options.B: Every 2 hours
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Only after delivery

explanation: During pushing (stage two), there's a lot of pressure! Checking every 5 minutes helps us catch any signs of distress immediately.

question: Which ethical principle means a nurse should actively do good and help the patient?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Justice

explanation: Nailed it! 'Beneficence' comes from words meaning to do good. It's your daily push as a nurse to take positive actions that genuinely help your patients.

question: When is it safe to upgrade a patient from clear fluids to full fluids?

options.A: Immediately upon admission before any assessment occurs
options.B: When the patient demands solid meat and fibrous vegetables
options.C: When the patient tolerates clear fluids without nausea or cramping
options.D: When the patient develops severe diarrhea from dairy products

explanation: We step things up gradually. If their tummy handles clear fluids well without vomiting or cramps, they are ready for the next level!

question: What is the main job of a vehicle when diluting a lotion?

options.A: To act as a safe base that mixes well with the active drug
options.B: To completely neutralize the active drug's healing properties
options.C: To add a strong fragrance to cover up chemical odors
options.D: To change a liquid medication into a hard tablet

explanation: Think of the vehicle as a friendly carrier base that helps you spread the active medicine evenly without fuss.

question: How does poverty directly affect a pregnant woman's health outcomes?

options.A: It forces healthcare providers to deny them basic vaccinations
options.B: It completely stops the placenta from producing progesterone and estrogen
options.C: It restricts their ability to afford transport and hospital fees during emergencies
options.D: It guarantees that they will develop gestational diabetes late in the third trimester

explanation: Financial barriers can prevent women from reaching skilled medical facilities when urgent complications arise. It's a reminder of why accessible healthcare is so vital.

question: What does the term 'oophoritis' mean?

options.A: Swelling of the fallopian tubes
options.B: Cyst formation on the cervix
options.C: Inflammation of the ovaries
options.D: Infection of the uterine lining

explanation: You've got this! Oophoritis simply means inflammation of one or both ovaries, usually caused by an infection. Great start!

question: Roughly what percentage of whole blood is made up of plasma?

options.A: About 55 percent
options.B: About 90 percent
options.C: About 25 percent
options.D: About 75 percent

explanation: Spot on! Plasma is the straw-colored liquid part of your blood, making up just over half (about 55%) of your total blood volume.

question: What is the incubation period of an infectious disease?

options.A: The period between receiving a vaccine and gaining immunity
options.B: The duration a patient remains infectious after recovery
options.C: The time between pathogen entry and the first symptom
options.D: The exact number of days a patient stays in the hospital

explanation: The incubation period starts when germs enter the body and ends when the very first signs of sickness appear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h1)

question: Why does lacking thiamine cause brain cells to die so quickly?

options.A: It disrupts critical energy pathways and glucose metabolism in neurons
options.B: It causes massive bacterial infections inside the cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: It triggers an autoimmune attack directly targeting the myelin sheath
options.D: It increases intracranial pressure by blocking the reabsorption of CSF

explanation: Think of thiamine as the spark plug for brain cells to burn glucose. Without it, the cells literally starve for energy and shut down.

question: A patient recovered from typhoid fever weeks ago, but lab tests still show they are shedding the bacteria. What type of carrier are they?

options.A: A chronic carrier
options.B: A clinical case
options.C: A healthy carrier
options.D: A convalescent carrier

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Someone who continues to carry and shed germs long after recovering from the illness is known as a chronic carrier.

question: Why are blood thinners frequently given to patients admitted with moderate to severe COVID-19?

options.A: To lower elevated blood pressure readings during a fever spike
options.B: To prevent dangerous blood clots caused by inflammation and immobility
options.C: To thin the thick mucus secretions blocking the upper airways
options.D: To improve the ability of red blood cells to carry extra oxygen

explanation: You got it! COVID-19 makes the blood prone to clotting, so giving thinners helps stop dangerous conditions like DVT or pulmonary embolism.

question: Why do pharmacologists group sedatives and hypnotics together?

options.A: They both depress the central nervous system depending on the dose
options.B: They both have zero risk of physical dependence
options.C: They are both used exclusively in emergency psychiatric settings
options.D: They are both derived from the same plant extracts

explanation: Both drug groups slow down the central nervous system. Whether they just calm you down or put you right to sleep usually depends on how much of the drug is given.

question: What happens to a reflex if the sensory neuron gets damaged or cut?

options.A: Only the integration center will process the signal.
options.B: The brain will take over the reflex function.
options.C: The reflex response will fail to occur.
options.D: The effector will react continuously without stopping.

explanation: Think of a reflex arc like a relay race. If one runner (the sensory neuron) drops out, the message never reaches the finish line and the reflex doesn't happen.

question: What is the main job of anti-spasmodic drugs in the tummy?

options.A: To coat the stomach lining and prevent acid ulcers
options.B: To kill harmful bacteria causing stomach infections
options.C: To speed up the transit time of stool in the colon
options.D: To relax overactive smooth muscle and relieve cramps

explanation: Think of anti-spasmodics as a calming massage for your gut muscles. They help stop those painful, tight cramps when the tummy muscles are working into overdrive!

question: About how fast does rapid-acting insulin start working after you inject it?

options.A: 10 to 15 minutes
options.B: 4 to 6 hours
options.C: 1 to 2 hours
options.D: 12 to 24 hours

explanation: Spot on! Rapid-acting insulin starts working almost immediately, which is why patients need to have their food ready right away.

question: Why do patients with skin problems easily get secondary bacterial infections?

options.A: They produce an excess amount of oils
options.B: Their immune systems are permanently shut down
options.C: Topical medications attract environmental toxins
options.D: Broken skin allows bacteria to enter deeper tissues

explanation: Spot on! When the skin has cracks or sores, the body loses its first line of defense, making it easy for bacteria to sneak in.

question: Which of these is a direct cause of maternal morbidity?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced diabetes
options.B: Chronic malaria infection
options.C: Severe sickle cell anemia
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Direct causes come straight from the obstetric process itself—like heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) right after childbirth. You'll see this often on the ward!

question: How does pharmacokinetic antagonism affect drug levels in a patient's body?

options.A: By binding permanently to every receptor in the nervous system
options.B: By changing the electrical charge of the red blood cells
options.C: By increasing the metabolism or excretion of the other drug
options.D: By stopping the kidneys from producing any urine output

explanation: One drug makes the body break down or flush out the other drug faster, leaving less active medicine floating around. Makes total sense when you break it down!

question: Which nursing action is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries and must be avoided?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands
options.B: Wearing clean gloves during procedures
options.C: Using single-dose medication vials
options.D: Performing hand hygiene before patient contact

explanation: Recapping used needles is a dangerous habit that frequently leads to accidental finger pricks. Keep safety first and drop them straight into the bin!

question: Which official body holds Nigerian nurses legally accountable for their practice?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: West African Health Organization
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: That's our umbrella body! The NMCN regulates nursing education and practice in Nigeria, keeping our profession standard and legal.

question: An older adult patient with orthostatic hypotension is preparing for discharge. What instruction should the nurse include in their care plan?

options.A: Avoid wearing compression socks because they block blood flow.
options.B: Drink less fluid during the day to avoid frequent bathroom trips.
options.C: Stand up as quickly as possible to get blood moving.
options.D: Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before standing up.

explanation: Sitting on the edge of the bed allows the cardiovascular system to adjust to posture changes, preventing orthostatic dizziness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h7)

question: What does 'Prior Informed Consent (PIC)' require before hazardous waste can be exported?

options.A: Approval from international shipping insurance companies
options.B: A public vote in the exporting nation's capital city
options.C: Written approval from the importing and transit countries
options.D: Permission from the World Health Organization director

explanation: You're doing great! PIC means any country receiving the waste—plus any countries the cargo passes through—must give their official written permission first.

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when trying to stop the spread of respiratory viruses in a hospital?

options.A: Reusing disposable single-use gloves between multiple patients
options.B: Ensuring proper room ventilation in clinical spaces
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.D: Cleaning high-touch environmental surfaces regularly

explanation: Single-use gloves are meant for one patient only! Reusing them is a sure way to spread germs around. You'd never make that mistake! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why might a patient with a badly damaged kidney have clear urine with no blood at all?

options.A: The blood supply or ureter to that kidney may be completely blocked or torn.
options.B: Blood from the injury goes directly into the stomach instead of the bladder.
