question: What is a major, life-threatening complication that can happen if bone infections are left untreated?

options.A: Permanent vision loss in both eyes
options.B: Total loss of stomach acid
options.C: Sepsis and septic shock
options.D: Sudden development of asthma

explanation: When an infection escapes the bone and enters the bloodstream, it can cause a whole-body emergency known as sepsis. Catching it early is key!

question: What is a vital nursing duty when managing a patient on peritoneal fluid exchange?

options.A: Checking the patient's blood pressure every five minutes
options.B: Disconnecting the sterile tubing system every two hours
options.C: Accurately recording the volume of fluid in and out
options.D: Massaging the patient's abdomen firmly to speed drainage

explanation: You got it! Keeping a strict fluid balance chart ensures the patient is draining out everything they put in and helps catch blockages early. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h5)

question: In Nigeria, under what single main condition is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: If fetal abnormalities are detected early
options.B: When requested by the parents of a minor
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: If the pregnancy resulted from financial hardship

explanation: Good to know for your exams and practice: Nigerian law is very strict and only permits abortion if it is done to preserve the mother's physical life.

question: Which nursing action is unsafe for a patient at high risk of bleeding?

options.A: Brushing teeth with a soft sponge
options.B: Using a sliding board for transfers
options.C: Checking urine output every shift
options.D: Taking a routine rectal temperature

explanation: Rectal thermometers can easily scratch the delicate lining down there and trigger bleeding. Always choose a safer route!

question: Why do we investigate an incident after a workplace injury happens?

options.A: To prove to external inspectors that the company has no safety rules
options.B: To find a way to punish the injured worker for being clumsy
options.C: To discover the root causes and prevent similar accidents from happening again
options.D: To increase the speed of production machinery in the factory

explanation: An incident investigation is never about blaming someone. It's about playing detective to fix the system so the exact same accident never happens to anyone else.

question: A patient is admitted with right-sided heart failure. Which physical sign is the nurse most likely to spot?

options.A: Flushed, warm skin and bounding pulses
options.B: Sudden high fever and severe headache
options.C: Bulging neck veins and swollen ankles
options.D: Clear lung sounds with no breathing trouble

explanation: Right-sided failure causes fluid to back up into the rest of the body. You'll often see this as swollen legs and distended neck veins!

question: A patient says they drink strong cough syrup containing codeine every day just to chill and relax. What is happening here?

options.A: Proper management of a chronic upper respiratory infection
options.B: Substance misuse and potential psychological dependence
options.C: An effective strategy to build natural immunity against colds
options.D: A harmless alternative to sleeping pills

explanation: Well done! Using codeine-lacking syrups just for a high or relaxation leads straight down the road to substance abuse and addiction.

question: Which of the following is NOT part of a nurse's everyday clinical responsibilities?

options.A: Educating the community on the importance of immunization
options.B: Synthesizing laboratory antibodies in a research facility
options.C: Monitoring patients for adverse reactions after vaccination
options.D: Recognizing early clinical signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Growing and building antibodies in a lab is work for researchers and scientists. Nurses focus on patient care, safety, and community health education!

question: Which stage of insect development is completely skipped when an insect goes through incomplete metamorphosis?

options.A: The egg stage
options.B: The adult stage
options.C: The pupal stage
options.D: The larval stage

explanation: Incomplete metamorphosis skips the resting pupa stage, moving straight from egg to nymph to adult. Simple and straightforward!

question: Which of these is NOT an infection prevention item found in a midwifery kit?

options.A: Alcohol-based hand rub for quick cleaning
options.B: A heavy-duty manual blood pressure cuff
options.C: Sterile and clean disposable gloves
options.D: A safety box for used needles

explanation: A blood pressure cuff is a vital tool for checking vitals, but it isn't an infection control supply like gloves or hand sanitizer.

question: A post-op patient presses a handheld button on their IV machine to release a safe dose of pain meds. What is this device called?

options.A: Enteral feeding pump
options.B: Large Volume Pump
options.C: Insulin ambulatory pump
options.D: Patient-Controlled Analgesia pump

explanation: That's right! A PCA pump lets patients safely manage their own pain within strict limits set by the care team.

question: Why do courts place so much legal weight on a patient's medication chart?

options.A: It determines how much tax the hospital pays to the government.
options.B: It acts as a contemporaneous legal record of the care provided.
options.C: It proves that the pharmaceutical manufacturer produced a safe drug.
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal testimony from the attending nurse.

explanation: Well done! Records written right when things happen ('contemporaneous') are trusted in court because human memory can fade over time.

question: What is the nurse's very first priority right after a baby is born?

options.A: To clean all the white cheesy stuff off the skin
options.B: To give the first routine vitamin K injection
options.C: To check if the newborn is vigorous and breathing well
options.D: To check the exact birth weight on a scale

explanation: As soon as a baby arrives, our main check is to see how well they are transitioning and if they need help taking their first breaths. You've got this!

question: Which electrical shift makes the heart muscle cells contract?

options.A: Hyperpolarization
options.B: Repolarization
options.C: Depolarization
options.D: Polarization

explanation: Depolarization is just the electrical spark where positive ions rush in, making the heart muscle squeeze!

question: What happens right after HIV DNA successfully joins the host cell's chromosomes?

options.A: The infected cell transforms directly into a malignant tumor cell
options.B: The virus destroys all antibodies circulating in the bloodstream
options.C: The host cell immediately undergoes programmed cell death
options.D: The host cell machinery begins producing viral proteins and RNA

explanation: Exactly! Once the viral DNA sneaks into the host's DNA, the host cell is tricked into manufacturing new copies of the virus. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h3)

question: What kind of data do you collect when running through the review of systems?

options.A: It documents surgical procedures performed in the past
options.B: It consists entirely of subjective data reported by the patient
options.C: It represents laboratory values collected from blood samples
options.D: It consists entirely of objective data measured by the nurse

explanation: You nailed it! Just like the rest of the history, this part is all about what the patient tells you they are experiencing.

question: Which category makes up the vast majority of all CJD cases?

options.A: Iatrogenic CJD
options.B: Variant CJD
options.C: Sporadic CJD
options.D: Familial CJD

explanation: Correct! Most CJD cases happen sporadically—meaning they appear out of nowhere for no known reason, without any inherited gene or infection link.

question: Which observation should you report to the physical therapist before their next session?

options.A: Normal vital signs measured before breakfast
options.B: The patient ate all of their afternoon meal
options.C: The patient slept well through the entire night
options.D: Severe pain or extreme fatigue during movement

explanation: If a patient is in too much pain or completely exhausted, the therapist needs to know so they can ease up on the routine.

question: A patient has a hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum (impaction), yet they keep passing small amounts of liquid. Why does this happen?

options.A: Infection has completely liquefied the entire colon
options.B: Liquid stool leaks around the solid blocked mass
options.C: The small intestine is hyperactive and rushing food
options.D: The kidneys are producing excessive fluid waste

explanation: Don't let this trick you in the ward! Liquid waste from higher up in the gut finds a way to slip past the hard, blocked stool, which can easily look like normal diarrhea.

question: When assessing muscle strength, how should the nurse evaluate the limbs?

options.A: By measuring the exact circumference with a tape
options.B: Bilaterally to compare both sides of the body
options.C: Only after administering pain medication
options.D: Only on the dominant side to save time

explanation: Comparing opposite sides helps identify localized weakness or asymmetry caused by neurological injury. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why should a nurse always wear gloves when applying a strong hormone cream to a patient's skin?

options.A: To keep the nurse's hands completely sterile during the procedure
options.B: To make sure the cream spreads more evenly across the patient's body
options.C: To prevent the nurse from absorbing the active drug through their own skin
options.D: To prevent the patient from feeling cold during the skin application

explanation: Topical medications can easily soak through your skin as you apply them. Wearing gloves protects you from accidentally absorbing active drugs into your own body!

question: What are vital statistics primarily records of?

options.A: Life events in a human population
options.B: Financial budgets of local clinics
options.C: Hospital equipment inventory
options.D: Nursing school enrollment numbers

explanation: Vital statistics focus strictly on tracking core life events such as births, deaths, and marriages within a community. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of these details must you include when charting steam tent therapy?

options.A: The brand name of the plastic tent canopy
options.B: The exact electrical voltage of the wall socket
options.C: The name of the manufacturer who built the bed
options.D: Start and end times of the treatment

explanation: You got it! Accurate start and end times give a clear timeline of the care you provided.

question: What are the two main ways misoprostol affects the uterus and cervix?

options.A: Decreasing blood flow and acting as local anesthesia
options.B: Stimulating contractions and causing cervical ripening
options.C: Blocking progesterone and shrinking the placenta
options.D: Paralyzing the muscle and closing the cervix tightly

explanation: Think of it as doing a two-step job: it softens the cervix so tissue can pass, and it helps the uterine muscle contract to push things out.

question: What part of the female reproductive system does a vulval tumour affect?

options.A: The external female genitalia
options.B: The glandular tissue of the cervix
options.C: The inner lining of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The muscular wall of the uterus

explanation: Vulval tumours specifically develop on the external structures of the female genitalia, such as the labia and clitoris. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: In what direction should you clean a female patient's perineal area before putting in a catheter?

options.A: From back to front
options.B: From side to side vigorously
options.C: From front to back
options.D: In a circular outward motion

explanation: Correct! Always wipe from front to back (toward the back passage) so you don't drag any germs from the anus toward the urethral opening.

question: Why is infection control often trickier in a patient's home compared to a hospital ward?

options.A: Standard precautions are legally prohibited in private residences
options.B: The environment is dynamic and outside direct professional control
options.C: Clients in homes always carry more dangerous bacteria
options.D: Hospitals lack the sanitation resources found in households

explanation: Every home is different! Unlike a controlled hospital room, you have family members, pets, and unique layouts to navigate. Keep up the great thinking!

question: Why do normal lab test values change when a woman is pregnant?

options.A: Pregnant women have a slower metabolic rate overall
options.B: Blood cells shrink in size during the first trimester
options.C: The laboratory equipment is calibrated differently for women
options.D: Pregnancy hormones significantly alter baseline body chemistry

explanation: Think of pregnancy as a total body makeover! Because hormones shift so much, the normal lab ranges you use for non-pregnant patients simply don't apply here.

question: Why do babies of young mothers often face more malnutrition and infections as they grow?

options.A: Breast milk produced by teenagers is naturally toxic to infants
options.B: Cultural laws forbid young mothers from feeding their babies solid foods
options.C: Infants born to young mothers have stronger immune systems that reject food
options.D: The young mother often lacks the knowledge, resources, and autonomy for proper childcare

explanation: Correct! Inexperience and a lack of support make it hard for young mums to provide the best care and nutrition.

question: How should you position your patient right after a thoracentesis is finished?

options.A: On the unaffected side
options.B: Prone on the abdomen
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: Flat on the affected side

explanation: You nailed it! Having them lie on the good (unaffected) side helps the tiny puncture site seal up and lets the treated lung expand fully.

question: A nurse washes her hands thoroughly with soap and water before entering a patient's room. Which group of germs is she mostly trying to wash away?

options.A: Resident microbiota
options.B: Systemic pathogens
options.C: Endogenous spores
options.D: Transient microbiota

explanation: Spot on! When you touch door handles or charts, you pick up temporary ('transient') microbes. Handwashing washes those casual hitchhikers right down the drain before you touch your patient.

question: What type of care usually triggers automatic DRF exemptions during an emergency?

options.A: Long-term physical therapy
options.B: Annual medical fitness checkups
options.C: Emergency trauma resuscitation
options.D: Routine elective cosmetic surgery

explanation: When every second counts, emergency trauma care gets fast-tracked so lifesaving supplies are never delayed by paperwork.

question: A patient scheduled for discharge is crying and upset after a new diagnosis. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Postpone detailed instructions until the patient's emotional readiness improves
options.B: Ask a family member to take over all future health responsibilities
options.C: Hand the patient a textbook and tell them to read it alone
options.D: Proceed quickly with the teaching so the patient leaves on time

explanation: Well reasoned! High emotions block learning. Comforting the patient and waiting until they are calmer is always the right clinical call.

question: Which activity must occur before an HIV test is administered to a client?

options.A: Pre-test counselling
options.B: Public community notification
options.C: Mandatory partner isolation
options.D: Immediate antiretroviral drug loading

explanation: Pre-test counselling prepares the client mentally and ensures they understand the testing process and their rights. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h2)

question: Why is it important to pick the right statistical test for your research data?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take their medications if the math is wrong
options.B: Ethical boards will fine the nursing unit for messy spreadsheets
options.C: Using the wrong test can lead to false conclusions and bad clinical practices
options.D: Hospital computers will crash if you select an improper formula

explanation: Right on target. Different questions need different math tools; using the wrong one gives misleading answers that could affect patient care.

question: What kind of muscle makes up the external anal sphincter?

options.A: Smooth muscle
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Skeletal muscle
options.D: Elastic cartilage

explanation: Because the outer sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, you have voluntary control over it. It's what lets you hold it in until you reach a toilet!

question: A patient reports hot flashes, night sweats, and irregular cycles. Which body systems are these complaints linked to?

options.A: Endocrine and reproductive systems
options.B: Musculoskeletal system
options.C: Gastrointestinal system
options.D: Respiratory system

explanation: You've got this! Hot flashes and night sweats happen when estrogen levels shift, which ties directly back to our hormone (endocrine) and reproductive systems.

question: What is one big problem with planting the exact same crop over and over again on a massive scale (monoculture)?

options.A: It automatically stops all rainfall in the region
options.B: It can deplete specific soil nutrients and attract pests
options.C: It completely prevents any food from growing
options.D: It causes crops to turn poisonous to humans

explanation: Growing just one type of plant drains certain minerals right out of the dirt and sends out an open invitation to pests that love that specific plant.
